newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A hefty dollar order by a single London-based bank late in the afternoon added to earlier local importer and other offshore dollar buying to push the rand four cents weaker on Friday.
At the local 1400 GMT close, the rand was quoted at 4.4370/4400 against the dollar after touching a day's weakest level of 4.4420 bid and compared with 4.3940/3970 on Thursday.
The currency was under pressure from the morning opening, as a weaker bond market combined with mid-month importer demand pushed it to over the 4.42 level before midday.
In the afternoon session, a dollar order in the region of $70 to $90 million, which one dealer said appeared to be linked to the unwinding of a short position, hit the currency.
Its woes were compounded by the fact that many other players had stayed short during the day in anticipation of Reserve Bank assistance as the currency weakened.
This failed to materialise, forcing the shorts to cover and leaving the currency five cents weaker at one point.
But comments by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals towards the close helped the rand regain some composure.
He told parliament's finance committee that the rand appeared relatively stable at around the 4.40 level against the dollar.
"Stals came out with the comment about the 4.40 level which stopped the upward movement," a senior trader said.

Dealers that the currency's move on the day was being viewed as a correction after its recent gains and that it was likely to resume it stronger trend next week, with initial targets set at 4.4250 against the dollar.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.0807/0899 against sterling from 7.0239/0331 overnight and at 0.3836/3840 marks from 0.3863/3867 previously.

The bond market also retraced some of its losses but was still sharply weaker on the day after the market was hit by heavy offshore selling amid fears of a hike in U.S. interest rates in the near future.
At 1400 GMT, the rand was pegged at 14.915 percent -- off an earlier high of 14.96 percent, but up from 14.66 percent late on Thursday.

Dealers said better-than expected February U.S. PPI data, which fell 0.4 percent month-on-month, helped the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury pull back from the 6.96 percent level reached overnight to 6.94 percent late on Friday afternoon.
After the day's shake-out, dealers said the market was expected to resume its recent bull trend, which would see yields move steadily lower next week.

Some traders felt, however, that the market had more room to weaken and said the key 15.00 percent level could be a target in the week ahead, although buyers were expected to surface if the market got that far.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates held steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate maintained its recent 15.90 to 16.10 percent range.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 10.890 billion rand on Thursday from 11.223 billion rand on Wednesday.
Bond Exchange data showed foreigners were net buyers of 792.46 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 554.24 on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on Thursday, settlement day, were 49.3 billion rand from 16.25 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
